changelog: v5.2 — crowd_deconcentrate becomes a continuous ramp instead of a binary gate. Crossing crowd>0.6 previously snapped top_k 4->8 AND max_weight_pct 30->25 simultaneously — the one cliff in the concentration stack whose CONSEQUENCE at its boundary is large (cluster_cap's cap engagement is self-smoothing by contrast: it trims TO the cap, so a cluster at cap+eps is trimmed by eps). Now the response scales 0->1 across crowd in [0.40, 1.20]: max_weight_pct interpolates continuously and top_k steps one name at a time. 40% of reallocations land in a partial response the gate could not express (top_k now spreads k4:25 k5:37 k6:26 k7:9 k8:4). 2026-01 is the case in point: crowd 58% sat just under the old gate and got NOTHING; it now gets a 0.23 response. vs v5.1: CAGR 18.31->18.49%, Martin 3.703->3.750, sCopley 2.028->2.059, turnover 4.782->4.699 with 123 fewer trades and lower cost drag. Mechanism: the ramp is LESS reactive in moderate crowding, where the binary gate over-reacted by jumping straight to full response. ACCEPTANCE, reported in full including the parts that are not clean — diff:holdings run FIRST this time (books gently different, sum of held-period deltas +4.71pp in the candidate's favour); concentration identical (p90 30.0%, zero months above 40%); stress gate passes with ddExceedanceUlcer 0.02268->0.02227; D6 is MIXED (longest-underwater 1591d unchanged, start-cohorts-behind 20.62->16.77% much better, but RDD3y 0.057->0.060 and worst-3y-excess -39.36->-41.70% both slightly worse); both-halves is second-half-weighted (H1 Martin -0.038, H2 +0.188). D6's own language is about cohorts left behind, which is the instrument that improves; the average-lag statistics drift slightly the other way. Minor bump: this changes an existing lever's response SHAPE, not the mechanism set. Full record: docs/history/the-walk/the-walk-v5.md.
